# Badger

> Badger is a statically typed language for services and automation. The `badger` tool checks a program, compiles it with Cranelift, and runs it in-process on the Badger runtime (lightweight tasks, channels, lifecycle-managed systems, typed interceptor pipelines). Sources are `.bdg` files; a project has a `badger.toml`.

Points that differ from languages you may know:

- `x |> f(a)` means `f(x, a)`: the piped value is the first argument.
- Strings have no `+`; use interpolation, `$"{name} is {age}"`.
- `pub` functions must state parameter and result types; private ones may leave them to inference.
- Records (`{ name: "Ada" }`) are structural; `struct` and `enum` are nominal. Type names start uppercase; values, fields, functions, and variants start lowercase.
- No implicit numeric conversions: widen with `T.from`, narrow with `T.try_from` (a `Result`). Integer overflow stops the task.
- Errors are values: `Option`, `Result`, and `?`. Effects (`Io`, `Spawn`, ...) are part of function types and are checked.
- No or-patterns in `match` and no named or default arguments.
- `badger check PATH` prints nothing on success. `badger explain diagnostic E0301` explains a diagnostic code. `badger query api std.list` prints a module's public interface as JSON.
- `badger mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server (a persistent REPL session, checking, queries, runs); see the MCP reference.

## Learn

- [Learn Badger in 30 minutes](docs/tour.md): one commented walk through the language, every program checked and its output shown.
- [Guide index](docs/guide/README.md): ten chapters, one topic each.
- [Values and functions](docs/guide/01-values-and-functions.md): literals, bindings, operators, functions, lambdas, pipes, control flow.
- [Types and records](docs/guide/02-types-and-records.md): records, structs, enums, patterns, protocols, methods, generics.
- [Errors](docs/guide/03-errors.md): Option, Result, `?`, the Error protocol, defects.
- [Collections](docs/guide/04-collections.md): List, Map, Set, Array, Bytes, Seq, Stream.
- [Modules and projects](docs/guide/05-modules-and-projects.md): imports, visibility, `badger.toml`, dependencies.
- [Tasks and channels](docs/guide/06-tasks-and-channels.md): task scopes, cancellation, timeouts, channels, broadcast.
- [Effects and ownership](docs/guide/07-effects-and-ownership.md): effect rows, Transfer and Share, affine values, scoped regions.
- [Systems and pipelines](docs/guide/08-systems-and-pipelines.md): typed systems with lifecycles, interceptor pipelines.
- [Testing and contracts](docs/guide/09-testing-and-contracts.md): `badger test`, std.test, `requires`/`ensures`, record and replay.
- [Services](docs/guide/10-services.md): HTTP, databases, configuration, logging, releases.

## Reference

- [Standard library](docs/api/README.md): every standard module, generated from the checked interfaces (`badger doc std`).
- [CLI](docs/reference/cli.md): every `badger` command and flag.
- [REPL](docs/reference/repl.md): the interactive session and its commands.
- [MCP server](docs/reference/mcp.md): tools, arguments, and results of `badger mcp`.
- [Configuration](docs/reference/config.md): `badger.toml`, `badger.lock`, runtime settings, `BADGER_*` environment variables.
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): all docs, including topic notes.

- [Grammar](spec/grammar.ebnf): EBNF grammar.
